story: The New Haven Green is a 16-acre park that was completed in 1638. It is the central square of the nine-square plan that colonist John Brockett designed and surveyed for the Puritan settlers. In its early years it was called 'the marketplace' and held a watch house, a prison and a school.

For its first 150 years, the Green was the main burial ground for New Haven. The practice ended by 1821 and many headstones were moved to Grove Street Cemetery, but the remains were not. Between 4,000 and 5,000 people are estimated to still lie beneath the soil.
Three early 19th-century churches stand on the upper Green. They are the reason the Green was designated a National Historic Landmark District in 1970.
stops.fact: The Puritans said to have sized the Green for 144,000 people.
stops.disputed: Many people say the Puritans designed the Green for the number they believed would be spared in the Second Coming of Christ. Wikipedia says they were 'said to' have done it, which is a legend, not a record.

claims.t: All the graves were moved off the Green.
claims.why: Wikipedia says the headstones were moved but the remains were not.

story: The Old Campus is the oldest part of the Yale University campus. It is a 4-acre (1.6 ha) courtyard with a main entrance from the New Haven Green known as Phelps Gate. Fourteen buildings surround it, including eight dormitories and two chapels.

Yale's first building here, the College House, went up in 1718. Connecticut Hall followed in 1750 and is Yale's only surviving building from the colonial era. A plan in 1792 called Old Brick Row was the first campus plan in the United States and became a template for many other American colleges.
After 1870, the Old Brick Row plan gave way to the current quadrangle. Architect Charles C. Haight finished Phelps Gate in 1895 and Phelps Hall in 1896.
stops.fact: The first U.S. campus plan was drawn up here in 1792.
stops.disputed: Many people think old colleges just grew without a plan. Wikipedia says the 1792 Old Brick Row plan was the first campus plan in the United States.

claims.t: Connecticut Hall is Yale's only surviving building from the colonial era.
The Old Brick Row plan from 1792 is still how the campus looks today.
claims.why: Wikipedia says it gave way to the current quadrangle after 1870.

story: Vanderbilt Hall on Yale's Old Campus was completed in 1894. It was designed by Charles Coolidge Haight, an architect from New York City who also designed most of the buildings at Columbia College's old campus on Madison Avenue.

Haight designed many buildings at Yale. Phelps Gate followed Vanderbilt Hall in 1895, and Phelps Hall in 1896. Yale's collegiate Gothic look is more often credited to the better-known James Gamble Rogers, but many of Haight's buildings survive.

This is a good place to see the contrast. The 1901 photo shows the tall dorm with a tinted sky and cobbles, and the modern photo shows a lamp post and a stone gate post where the old street scene was.
stops.fact: Haight finished Phelps Gate in 1895, one year after Vanderbilt Hall.
stops.disputed: Many people think Yale's Gothic look is all by one architect. Wikipedia says Rogers is better known, but Haight designed many of the survivors.

claims.why: Wikipedia's list of Haight's works says so.

claims.t: Yale's Gothic buildings were all designed by James Gamble Rogers.
claims.why: Wikipedia says Haight designed numerous Yale buildings too.

story: The building at 67 High Street was built between 1842 and 1846 as the Yale College Library, the university's first freestanding library. Henry Austin designed it in the Gothic Revival style, with a two-story reading room under a hammer-beam ceiling.

A different Dwight Hall was built on the Old Campus in 1886 for the Yale YMCA. It was a brownstone building with a round tower, and it was torn down in 1926 so people could see the new Harkness Tower without anything in the way.
After that, the Dwight Hall organization moved into the old library and the name came with it. In 1930 and 1931 the reading room was turned into Dwight Chapel.
stops.fact: The original Dwight Hall was demolished in 1926 for a better view of Harkness Tower.
stops.disputed: Many people assume a building's name always goes with its first use. Wikipedia says the name moved here from a demolished building.

claims.t: The building was Yale's first freestanding library.
